## Why this unit matters

- Jump-process chapter: aggregate counts, "what happens next, to how many?"
- Agent-based chapter: individuals, but a fixed time step $\Delta t = 0.1$.
- Discrete-event simulation (DES): individuals **and** a continuous clock —
  jump directly from one scheduled event to the next, no discretization.
- Built two ways here: Agents.jl's `EventQueueABM`, and the general-purpose,
  process-oriented `ConcurrentSim.jl`.

::: {.notes}
Position this as the synthesis unit: same underlying CTMC as the
jump-process chapter, but resolved per individual, which is what lets it
express a fixed delay directly — no history function required.
:::

## Model assumptions and classification

Usual baseline: $N=1000$, $S(0)=990$, $I(0)=10$, $R(0)=0$, $c=10$,
$\beta=0.05$, $\gamma=0.25$. Each individual's next contact and recovery are
scheduled as events; the clock jumps to the next event anywhere in the
population.

| Property | Classification |
|---|---|
| Determinism | Stochastic |
| Time | Continuous, event-driven (no fixed $\Delta t$) |
| State | Discrete (individual status) |
| Representation | Individual-level |

## Equations

$$
T_\text{contact} \sim \mathrm{Exponential}(1/c), \qquad
\Pr(\text{infect} \mid \text{contact w/ infectious}) = \beta
$$
$$
T_\text{recovery} \sim \mathrm{Exponential}(1/\gamma)
$$

By memorylessness and superposition of independent Poisson processes, the
*population-level* counting process is exactly the jump-process CTMC; the
event-queue view additionally retains *who* infected *whom* and *when*.

## Julia API: `EventQueueABM`

```julia
using Agents

@agent struct Person(NoSpaceAgent)
    status::Symbol
end

transmit_propensity(a, m)  = a.status == :S ? m.c : 0.0
recovery_propensity(a, m)  = a.status == :I ? m.γ : 0.0

events = (AgentEvent(action! = transmit!, propensity = transmit_propensity),
          AgentEvent(action! = recover!,  propensity = recovery_propensity))
model = EventQueueABM(Person, events; properties, rng)
run!(model, tf; adata = [(:status, infected)])
```

By default an `AgentEvent`'s `timing` samples an exponential wait
parameterized by its `propensity` — matching the equations above exactly.

## Julia API: `ConcurrentSim.jl`

```julia
using ConcurrentSim, ResumableFunctions

@resumable function live(sim, person, m, rng)
    while person.status == :S
        @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.c)))
        alter = rand(rng, m.people)
        alter.status == :I && rand(rng) < m.β && (person.status = :I)
    end
    if person.status == :I
        @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.γ)))
        person.status = :R
    end
end
```

Not agent-centric: coroutine `@resumable` processes plus `Resource`/`Store`
primitives for queueing and contention — more bookkeeping, more generality.

## Generated result

```{julia}
#| label: fig-slide-a03-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Single EventQueueABM and ConcurrentSim realisations against the deterministic ODE mean field."
#| echo: false

using Agents, ConcurrentSim, ResumableFunctions, Random, Distributions, OrdinaryDiffEq, CairoMakie

const β = 0.05; const c = 10.0; const γ = 0.25; const N = 1000; const I0 = 10; const tf = 40.0

@agent struct Person(NoSpaceAgent)
    status::Symbol
end
function transmit!(agent, model)
    alter = random_agent(model)
    if alter.status == :I && (rand(abmrng(model)) ≤ model.β)
        agent.status = :I
    end
end
recover!(agent, model) = (agent.status = :R)
transmit_propensity(agent, model) = agent.status == :S ? model.c : 0.0
recovery_propensity(agent, model) = agent.status == :I ? model.γ : 0.0
infected(x) = count(==(:I), x)

properties = Dict(:β => β, :c => c, :γ => γ)
events = (AgentEvent(action! = transmit!, propensity = transmit_propensity),
          AgentEvent(action! = recover!, propensity = recovery_propensity))
eq_model = EventQueueABM(Person, events; properties, rng = Xoshiro(20250711))
for i in 1:N
    add_agent!(Person(; id = i, status = i <= I0 ? :I : :S), eq_model)
end
eq_data, _ = run!(eq_model, tf; adata = [(:status, infected)])

mutable struct SIRPerson
    id::Int
    status::Symbol
end
mutable struct SIRModel
    sim::Simulation; β::Float64; c::Float64; γ::Float64
    ta::Vector{Float64}; Ia::Vector{Int}; people::Vector{SIRPerson}
end
@resumable function live(sim, person, m, rng)
    while person.status == :S
        @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.c)))
        alter = rand(rng, m.people)
        if alter.status == :I && rand(rng) < m.β
            person.status = :I
            push!(m.ta, now(sim)); push!(m.Ia, count(p -> p.status == :I, m.people))
        end
    end
    if person.status == :I
        @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.γ)))
        person.status = :R
        push!(m.ta, now(sim)); push!(m.Ia, count(p -> p.status == :I, m.people))
    end
end
sim = Simulation()
people = [SIRPerson(i, i <= I0 ? :I : :S) for i in 1:N]
cs_model = SIRModel(sim, β, c, γ, [0.0], [I0], people)
cs_rng = Xoshiro(20250711)
for person in cs_model.people
    @process live(cs_model.sim, person, cs_model, cs_rng)
end
run(cs_model.sim, tf)

function sir_ode!(du, u, p, t)
    S, I, R = u; β, c, γ = p; Ntot = S + I + R
    λ = β * c * I / Ntot
    du[1] = -λ * S; du[2] = λ * S - γ * I; du[3] = γ * I
end
sol_ode = solve(ODEProblem(sir_ode!, [990.0, 10.0, 0.0], (0.0, tf), (β, c, γ)), Tsit5())

fig = Figure(size = (760, 400))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel = "time", ylabel = "infectious count")
stairs!(ax, eq_data.time, eq_data.infected_status; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 2, label = "I (EventQueueABM)")
stairs!(ax, cs_model.ta, cs_model.Ia; color = :steelblue, linewidth = 2, label = "I (ConcurrentSim)")
lines!(ax, sol_ode.t, sol_ode[2, :]; color = :black, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "I (ODE mean field)")
axislegend(ax; position = :rt)
fig
```

## Validation

- **Conservation**: every recorded row of both simulations sums to $N$.
- **Monotonicity**: the one-way $S \to I \to R$ transition keeps $S$
  non-increasing and $R$ non-decreasing in both implementations.
- **Ensemble check**: a 20-run `EventQueueABM` ensemble's mean final size is
  within 10% of the deterministic ODE prediction.

## Interpretation and limitations

- `EventQueueABM` automates scheduling but its default `adata` samples once
  per unit time — coarser than the true event resolution.
- `ConcurrentSim` needs hand-written recording, but every event is captured
  exactly when it happens, and its `Resource`/`Store` primitives extend to
  models with no natural agent-centric analogue (e.g. limited hospital beds).
- Both scale worse than the aggregated jump-process CTMC: scheduling
  $O(N)$ individual events costs more than resampling one aggregate draw.
- Neither requires exponential timing: `AgentEvent`'s `timing` and
  `ConcurrentSim`'s `timeout` both accept arbitrary — including fixed —
  waiting times, so a DES can encode the fixed delay of the DDE unit
  directly, with no history function or method of steps.

::: {.notes}
The fixed-delay exercise is the payoff line connecting this unit back to
the very first appendix: individual-level bookkeeping sidesteps the whole
history-function machinery because each agent just remembers its own
infection time.
:::

## Key takeaways

- DES resolves the same CTMC as the jump-process chapter, per individual,
  on a continuous event-driven clock.
- `EventQueueABM` (Agents.jl 7) and `ConcurrentSim.jl` are two current,
  complementary ways to build one: agent/event-centric vs. general
  process/resource-centric.
- A DES can express fixed delays and resource contention that are awkward
  or impossible in the population-level or fixed-$\Delta t$ models earlier
  in the course.
